trust_decision.summary: The REST integration decides that any request URL built from a query's path/queryString may carry the datasource's stored auth headers; the only origin decision in the tree happens later, in fetchWithBlacklist's redirect helper, which merely strips four fixed header names instead of refusing a cross-origin hop.

landing_point.why: The advisory names the REST datasource and credential theft; the first place an engineer looks is RestIntegration._req, where getAuthHeaders() output is merged into this.headers and handed to the fetch helper.

fix_sites.entry_point: fetchWithBlacklist (shared outbound HTTP primitive used by the REST integration and every automation step)
app query execution and automation Execute Query step

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The redirect helper already deletes Authorization/cookie headers on a cross-origin hop, so the shared backend-core fetch layer looks 'already handled'; and a REST-template datasource legitimately rewrites the base URL in the thread runner before the integration runs, so the integration cannot be sure what the real origin is.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate redirects must keep working: a same-origin 302 to a relative Location ("/next") is followed with the auth headers intact, and a datasource with no base URL relies on a query path that is already an absolute URL.

O6_input_shapes: path as a relative string resolved against datasource config.url
path as an already-absolute URL (getUrl only prefixes http:// when config.url is absent)
redirect Location as absolute cross-origin URL vs relative same-origin path
authConfigId/authConfigType pair: inline OAuth2 config vs stored OAuth2 config resolved by bare id
auth header as Authorization (basic/bearer) vs an arbitrary custom header name from the apiKey auth type

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Automation Execute Query step: an unauthenticated POST /api/webhooks/trigger/:instance/:id supplies the query parameters that the saved REST query interpolates, then the run goes through queryController.executeV2AsAutomation into RestIntegration._req with the datasource's stored auth headers.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Automation query parameters are considered trusted trigger input, and the step reuses the query controller rather than the datasource route the report describes.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different package path depth: automations/ vs integrations/ and api/controllers/query/

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Query-level authConfigId with authConfigType OAUTH2 resolves a stored OAuth2 config by bare id (getToken(id)) with no check that the config belongs to the datasource being executed, so a query on datasource A can attach datasource B's OAuth token to a request to any URL.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: authConfigId is treated as a datasource-scoped identifier, and a separate helper (getToken in the oauth2 sdk) is assumed to enforce ownership.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file but a different helper, whose failure surfaces in packages/server/src/sdk/workspace/oauth2/utils.ts:102-116

O8b_injection_room.sibling: apiKey auth type emitting an arbitrary header name that the redirect strip list does not cover
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The branch already exists for OpenAPI-imported datasources, so a maintainer adding a same-origin assertion that only inspects Authorization would leave it forwarding X-Api-Key credentials.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a configurable/extended sensitive-header list instead of a hard-coded four-name list
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Every call site (automation webhook steps, plugin github/npm, object store) passes its own headers through this primitive, so widening or parameterising the list is a natural next change.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second URL-rewriting path (applyBaseUrl for REST templates) that produces the effective origin after the integration's config was built
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The thread runner already rewrites fieldsClone.path from datasourceClone.config.url, so any origin check done inside the integration sees only the post-rewrite value.

O9_family: CWE-200 exposure of sensitive information (stored datasource credentials forwarded to a cross-origin request)

services: MinIO (only for server API/integration suites; the REST integration unit suite uses a mocked undici dispatcher)
